result.explanation: More than six years elapsed between the policy start date in January 2020 and the hospital admission in June 2026, which exceeds both the 36-month pre-existing disease waiting period and the 60-month moratorium period. However, coverage after 36 months under the pre-existing disease clause on page 30 requires that the condition was declared at inception, and the moratorium clause on page 37 requires 60 continuous months of coverage without a break. Because the provided records do not state whether the heart condition existed prior to 2020, whether it was declared on the application, or whether the policy was renewed continuously without a break, the claim cannot be adjudicated without these facts.
result.what_would_change_it: Proof of continuous policy renewal without any break from January 15, 2020 through June 10, 2026, along with confirmation of whether the condition was declared at policy inception.

arguments.insurer_position: Under the pre-existing disease exclusion clause on page 30 and definition on page 7, expenses related to a pre-existing condition are excluded until 36 months of continuous coverage elapse, and subsequent coverage requires that the condition was declared at application and accepted by the insurer. Although the policy inception date is January 15, 2020, the claimant has not established that the policy was continuously covered without a break as required by the waiting period definition on page 11, nor that the condition was declared and accepted at inception under the pre-existing disease clause on page 30. Consequently, the claim fails to meet the contractual prerequisites for coverage of a pre-existing condition.
arguments.claimant_position: The policy commenced on January 15, 2020, and the hospitalization occurred on June 10, 2026, which is more than six years later and well past the 36-month exclusion period outlined in the pre-existing disease clause on page 30. Furthermore, the insurer has not established that the condition met the definition of a pre-existing disease on page 7 prior to policy inception. In addition, because over sixty continuous months have elapsed since inception, the claim is protected under the moratorium period clause on page 37.
arguments.insurer_weak_point: More than six years elapsed between the policy start date in January 2020 and the hospitalization in June 2026, which well exceeds the 36-month waiting period and 60-month moratorium period, making the rejection unsustainable unless the insurer proves a break in continuous coverage or non-disclosure.
arguments.claimant_weak_point: The insurer may argue that the policy was not continuously renewed without a break or that the sum insured was recently enhanced, which would restart the waiting period for the enhanced amount under the pre-existing disease clause on page 30.

result.explanation: The pre-existing diseases exclusion clause on page 30 excludes coverage for pre-existing conditions and their direct complications until 36 months of continuous coverage have elapsed from the policy inception date. With your policy commencing on January 1, 2025, and admission occurring in June 2026, only 17 months of continuous coverage had passed at the time of your angioplasty. Provided the insurer has medical evidence that your cardiac condition was diagnosed or treated prior to policy inception, the rejection under the 36-month waiting period is supported by the policy wording. However, the exclusion cannot stand if the condition arose for the first time after your policy began.
result.what_would_change_it: Medical evidence showing the heart condition was first diagnosed after January 1, 2025, or a policy schedule showing ported prior coverage credits or an opted reduced 12-month waiting period.

arguments.insurer_position: Under the pre-existing disease clause on page 7 and the waiting period clause on page 11, pre-existing conditions and their treatments are excluded from coverage until all mandatory waiting periods are completed. The pre-existing diseases exclusion clause on page 30 mandates a waiting period of 36 months of continuous coverage from the policy inception date before expenses related to pre-existing diseases and their direct complications become payable. Because the policy commenced on January 1, 2025, and the angioplasty took place in June 2026, only 17 months of coverage had elapsed, rendering the claim non-payable under the policy terms.
arguments.claimant_position: If the angioplasty treatment arose from underlying chronic conditions such as high blood pressure or cholesterol, it is covered under the ABCD Chronic Care clause on page 69 after a 30-day waiting period, which was fully satisfied between policy inception on January 1, 2025, and admission in June 2026. Furthermore, if the policyholder transferred prior continuous coverage credits under the portability clause on page 7 or elected a reduced waiting period under the PED waiting period modification clause on page 26, the standard 36-month exclusion period is reduced or waived. Consequently, the insurer cannot summarily reject the claim under the standard pre-existing disease exclusion without accounting for these specific coverage terms.
arguments.insurer_weak_point: The insurer bears the burden of proving that the insured's cardiac condition requiring angioplasty was actually diagnosed, treated, or advised upon prior to policy inception to qualify as a pre-existing disease.
arguments.claimant_weak_point: The insurer may argue that angioplasty is a procedure for coronary artery disease rather than direct management of blood pressure or cholesterol, and that the claimant has provided no evidence of an opted PED modification or ported prior continuous coverage to shorten the 36-month waiting period.

arguments.insurer_position: The insurer appropriately capped the claim for cataract surgery because the policy explicitly limits coverage for cataract treatment to 25% of the Sum Insured or Rs. 40,000, whichever is lower, per eye in a policy year, as stated in the cataract treatment clauses on page 9 and page 22. arguments.claimant_position: The insurer partially rejected the claim by invoking a sub-limit, but it has not established the policy's Sum Insured or whether the procedure was performed on one eye or both eyes.
